orders: The module SECURITY docstring contains the verbatim sentence "This module issues GET only -- _http_get". That is now FALSE: this slice added _http_post, the module's sole writer, which POSTs a comment to a live work item. The plan-critic flagged this exact line at critique time as a safety defect fixable in one revision, and it survived the fix round. Rewrite it to state the truth: the READ lane issues GET only and is structurally incapable of a mutating verb (no `data` parameter on _http_get), while ONE separate writer, _http_post, issues exactly one mutating verb - POST to the work-item comments collection - and only when armed by --post. Do not weaken any other sentence in that docstring.

The top-level argparse description is the verbatim string "Azure DevOps Services work-item reader (read-only)." Every user of `ado_client.py --help` reads it, and it is false for a CLI that now exposes `comment --post`, which mutates a work item with no delete lane. Replace it so it names both lanes and says the write is off by default - for example a reader plus a bounded comment writer armed only by --post. This is the operator's first and often only description of what the tool can do.

The test module docstring opens with the verbatim line "Tests for the read-only Azure DevOps work-item reader (stdlib unittest)." and later claims it covers "the READ-ONLY" guarantee. This same file now contains the entire write lane's test surface, so the docstring understates what is tested and repeats the false read-only framing. Update it to describe both lanes, keeping the accurate clause that the GET helper has no `data` parameter as a property of the READ lane specifically.

_assert_target_unchanged's docstring claims "the environment check" "catches the org moving between the preview invocation and the armed one". The reviewer demonstrated that branch is unreachable in production: resolve_work_item stamps record['org'] from the same credentials() read that produced `org`, so the first assert_same_target already proves target[0] == org and the second call is a no-op on every real input. Rewrite the docstring so it does not tell a reader a protection exists on a path no production input reaches - say plainly that the record check catches BOTH drift shapes and that the environment comparison is belt-and-braces against a future change that stops deriving the record's org from the same read. Keep the check itself; only the prose is wrong.
